R371.note: Checks bytesRead but handles a short read by rejecting with 400 instead of filling the buffer (loop or Stream.ReadAtLeast), so a legitimate upload whose first Read returns fewer than 8 bytes is now refused, and the write-up does not say so.

R372.note: Function constructor replaced by expr-eval-fork Parser closes code execution, but ast.evaluate(order) exposes {total, tax} as top-level variables, so the contract's own example order.total + order.tax throws 'undefined variable: order' (needs evaluate({ order })) - legitimate previews now 500 and the write-up claims failure semantics are unchanged (judged from expr-eval's evaluate() variable lookup, not run).

R373.note: Strict in_array allowlist of exactly the four renderer macro verbs before $renderer->$macro(); the allowlist is the product-defined token set so no legitimate macro is rejected.

R374.note: parseClaimsJwt replaced with setSigningKey(key).parseClaimsJws(token), valid on jjwt 0.11.5; the new required SecretKey constructor argument and the catch-and-continue-unauthenticated behaviour for bad tokens are both stated in the write-up.

R375.note: HMAC-over-payload plus restricted find_class is the right idea, but it ships a hardcoded fallback key 'default-dev-key' (forgeable whenever the env var is unset) and a broad numpy/sklearn/pandas/__main__ prefix allowlist; every existing unsigned pickle from the unchanged nightly job now fails verification with a 500, which the write-up discloses as a required producer change.

R376.note: count > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(ProductRow) guard before the multiply, freeing batch and returning NULL, closes the overflow and preserves the stated contract; the extra limits.h include is harmless.

R377.note: realpath() then separator-aware str_starts_with containment check before file_get_contents closes traversal; failure paths return the same 404 the original produced for unreadable files.

R378.note: Signature verification enabled with pinned HS256 and required account_id claim closes the forgery, but the fix hardcodes a placeholder secret in source, and ExpiredSignatureError/MissingRequiredClaimError (InvalidTokenError, not DecodeError) are uncaught so those tokens now produce a 500 instead of 401.

R379.note: Prefix-with-separator containment check on the cleaned joined path rejects escapes with a 403 (stated) and leaves every in-root filename working; os.Root/filepath.IsLocal would be stronger against symlinks but the lexical check closes the reported sink.

R380.note: Resulting code is a PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder and setString binding, so the sink is parameterized and nothing else changes - but note the case file was already in exactly this form; the write-up's diff is a whitespace no-op and its claim that the original concatenated input is false.

R381.note: Files.probeContentType replaced with Tika.detect(Path) against the same allowlist, dependency stated, temp file cleaned on the new error path; the client extension is still kept on the temp file so Tika can fall back to name hints for content it does not recognise, though HTML/SVG/script content is still caught by magic detection.

R382.note: Markup(label) replaced with html.escape(label) so the label renders as text; status is a stub constant and nothing else in the response changes.

R383.note: PDO prepare with ? placeholder and execute([$sku]) replaces concatenation; the added execute() false check maps to the same null/404 outcome the original produced for a failed query.

R384.note: Field allowlist plus ORM filter(tenant_id=..., field__icontains=term) keeps tenant and term bound and rejects raw identifiers as the contract requires; the specific approved set (email/name/phone/company/address) is the write-up's guess and should be confirmed against the Customer model, and icontains now escapes % and _ in the term.

R385.note: resolve_entities=False on the lxml XMLParser is the prescribed fix for this sink; only internal entity expansion in legitimate documents changes, which is the standard accepted trade-off.

R386.note: verify() return value is now checked and a false result throws JOSEException before claims are read; a 401 response would be a cleaner rejection than an unhandled exception, but valid tokens are unaffected.
